details:
Currently, if you want to play a game in VRChat, you have to go to a world that has that game. This works well for games where the world itself is a play area, or where you need lots of space to play. But there's also a category of smaller games that don't really depend on the world around them, like board games, billiards, arcade machines, etc. Many of these are already distributed as prefabs that world creators can place anywhere. But as a player, if you want to play chess, you still can't simply drop a chessboard wherever you want - you have to go to a world that has one. This is inconvenient for both players and world creators.

For players, the problem is that people hanging out together in a group can't easily do different activities at the same time. If two people want to play chess or some other mini-game, they have to leave whatever everyone else is doing, or hope the rest of the group will follow them. But some people might not be interested in that game and would get bored; others might be afk and wonder where everyone went; some simply don't want to move or interrupt their conversation. Changing worlds introduces a lot of friction.

It is also inconvenient for world creators. If you want to make a simple game, you also have to build a whole world around it, even though the world itself might have nothing to do with the game. Or the opposite - if you're a designer who enjoys making beautiful worlds, you still need to think about what games and activities to add so players won't get bored. Different people are good at different things, but the current system pushes them to make stuff that is not really related to the stuff they actually want to make. Allowing players to bring any game into any world would add a lot of flexibility and let creators focus on what they're good at.

How would it work? I imagine portable games working similarly to placeable items: you select one from the menu, point at the ground, and it spawns there. But unlike items who are designed to be lightweight and optimized, portable games can have all the stuff you'd typically find in a world prefab - udon, physics, networking, video playback, etc. That could be a lot of stuff, so the games should not be loaded automatically for everyone. Instead, other players would see a small orb, similar to a sharing pedestal, that describes the activity, and provides a button to download and load it into the world.  Game creators could include a button to unload the game and turn it back into an orb. Alternatively, players could see a list of currently loaded activities in their menu, with an option to unload any of them.

The game shouldn't disappear when the player who spawned it leaves the instance, since other people might still be playing it. The orb should disappear only when nobody in the instance has the activity loaded anymore.

Portable games should also have access to the same monetization features available to their creators in their own worlds, such as supporter subscriptions with unlockable benefits. This would open up an entirely new market within VRChat: a marketplace for world prefabs and mini-games, which currently exists only outside VRChat.
title: Portable Games (Activities)
